Maine Education Policy Research Institute
Testimony of Dr. Amy Johnson, Maine Education Policy Research Institute (MEPRI)
Neither for Nor Against: L.D. 318, Resolve, Directing the Maine Education Policy Research Institute and the Maine Department of Education to Recommend Changes to the Essential Programs and Services Funding Formula
Date: May 16, 2025
Dear Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs,
I am joining you today to speak neither for nor against L.D. 318.
The bill language requests that MEPRI conduct certain activities, most of which are a direct continuation of our work this year on the EPS formula. We would be glad to serve in that capacity if the Resolve is passed. The assigned tasks are feasible within the suggested timeframe.
In order to maximize this opportunity and to ensure that the Department has adequate time to conduct the scenarios, we propose two amendments:
1. Add as Section 1, item 1: "G. One or more options for incorporating a student economic disadvantage factor into the method for determining the amount of state subsidy provided to each town (i.e. adjusting the local required share of the EPS cost estimate based on the proportion of economically disadvantaged resident students)."
2. Change the first two deadlines in section 1 from August 15, 2025 to August 1, 2025.
In order to conduct the work within existing resources, we would need to have a portion of our FY2026 annual research contract with the Education Committee dedicated to the Resolve.
We can be available upon request to attend the work session to discuss the proposed study.

Sincerely,
Amy Johnson Co-Director, MEPRI

LD 318, An Act Regarding School Funding and General Purpose Aid for
Local Schools
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Aflairs
Good morning, Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy and fellow distinguished members of
the Joint Standing Cormnittee on Education and Cultural Affairs. My name is Michael Brennan,
and I represent House District 115, which includes a portion of Portland. Today, I am here to
introduce LD 318, An Act Regarding School Funding and General Purpose Aid for Local
Schools.
This bill directs the Maine Education Policy Research Institute (MEPRI) to specify certain elements of the essential programs and services funding formula to be simulated with new parameters. The Maine Department of Education (DOE) would be required to conduct
simulations of the proposed parameters. Further, MEPRI would be required to solicit feedback
from stakeholder representatives on the recommended potential adjustments to the funding formula in light of the forecasts prepared by the DOE.
Additionally, LD 318 would require the DOE to conduct the reviews within existing resources and MEPR1 to conduct the work within its budgeted contract. MEPRI and DOE would be
required to submit reports with their findings and recommendations to this committee no later than January 15, 2026.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I am happy to answer any questions.

District 115: Part of Portland

Sec. 1. Maine Education Policy Research Institute to further review certain essential programs and services components; report. Resolved: That the Maine Policy Education Research Institute shall:
1. Prior to August 15, 2025: Identify updated cost model parameters for the Maine Department of Education to use in simulating projected impacts. Parameters shall include, but are not limited to,
the following:
A. Transitional recommendations for moderating the special education component's
expenditure-based (Step 6) adjustment, which was found to be driving inequities within the
formula;
B. A minimum index value for the regional adjustment;
C. Recommendation for calculating a regional index based on a valid and reliable cost-of-living
measure(s);
D. An updated per-pupil amount to more adequately fund Instructional Staff Support;
E. A variable student weight for economic disadvantage, with higher-poverty units receiving a
progressively higher student weight; and
F. Alternative parameters and implementation guidelines for the transportation model.
2. Prior to August 15, 2025: identify additional information needed from SAUs, to be collected by the Department of Education in Fall 2025, to examine the per-pupil costs of certain high-cost indistrict special education programs and sen/ices;
3. Solicit stakeholder input on the results of simulations generated by the Department through
Section 2 and submit a report summarizing the recommended parameters and results of stakeholder feedback no later than January 15, 2026.
Sec. 2. Maine Department of Education to conduct simulations of updated parameters for certain essential programs and services components; report. Resolved: That the Maine Department of Education shall:
1. Simulate the impacts that the parameters proposed by MEPRI in Section 1 would have had on FY2026 EPS allocations, including the impact of all parameters combined, on the
following:
A. Total statewide cost of education B. Statewide mil rate expectation
C. Local and state shares and state share percentage of the EPS estimated cost of
education in each school administrative unit 2. Provide the results of the above simulations to the Maine Education Policy Research Institute
no later than October 15, 2025.

3. Submit a report summarizing the results of the above simulations, as well as any other
simulated changes the Commissioner of Education may recommend, by January 15, 2026.
The joint standing committee may submit legislation related to the report to the 132nd Legislature
in 2026.
The Maine Education Policy Research Institute shall conduct the above work within existing contracted resources. The Department of Education shall conduct the work within existing
resources.
SUMMARY
The resolve directs the Maine Education Policy Research Institute to specify certain elements of
the essential programs and services funding formula to be simulated with new parameters. The
Department of Education is required to conduct simulations of the proposed parameters. The Maine Education Policy Research Institute is required to solicit feedback from stakeholder representatives on the recommended potential adjustments to the funding formula in light of the forecasts prepared by the Department of Education.
The resolve directs the Department of Education to conduct the reviews within existing resources and the Maine Education Policy Research Institute to conduct the work within its budgeted contract.
The Maine Education Policy Research Institute and Maine Department of Education are required to submit reports with their findings and recommendations to the joint standing committee of the Legislature having jurisdiction over education matters no later than January 15, 2026.

Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and Distinguished Members of the Education and

LD 318, Resolve. Directing the Maine Education Policy Research Institute and the Maine
Department of Education to Recommend Changes to the Essential Programs and Services
Funding Formula, directs the Maine Policy Education Research Institute (MEPRI) to identify recommended changes to the Essential Programs and Services (EPS) funding formula by August 15, 2025, and for the Maine Department of Education (DOE) to conduct simulations of the recommendations of MEPRI by October 15, 2025, and with a report summarizing the results to be submitted to the Education and Cultural Affairs committee by January 15, 2026.
The resolve will require the Maine Education Policy Research Institute (MEPRI) to review and provide updated parameters for proposed changes to the Maine Department of Education
School Finance team so that they may run the simulations in the EPS formula to determine
overall impacts of proposed changes.
Those updated parameters and simulations are for the following sections of the Essential Programs and Services (EPS) funding formula:
A. Transitional recommendations for moderating the special education component's expenditure-based (Step 6) adjustment, which was found to be driving inequities within the formula.
Response: Per Title 20-A, �15681-A, subsection 2D, the maintenance of effort adjustment is not well defined in statute and recommendations for moderating it would likely improve the equity of the overall EPS allocation of state funding for education.
B. A minimum index value for the regional adjustment.
